Subject: SecureOps Pilot: VPC/KMS/Air-gap discovery — recap & next steps

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the time this morning — appreciated the clear run-through of SecureOps' constraints. Quick recap to make sure we captured everything and to outline proposed next steps. See short TL;DR below, details after.

TL;DR
- Primary goal: Evaluate Redwood Private for an air-gapped/PVC-enabled on-prem pilot to serve inference for PHI-scoped workloads.
- Key constraints: customer-managed KMS/HSM, no outbound internet from inference cluster, strict inbound firewall rules (Palo Alto), and quarterly audit/reporting requirements.
- Next steps: Security questionnaire (attached), architecture diagram from your infra team, and a technical kickoff for 6/6 or 6/7.

What we heard (pain points & success criteria)
- Data residency & isolation: All inference must run within SecureOps-controlled network; logs and telemetry must be retained on-site for 365 days and pulled into their SIEM.
- KMS/HSM: Keys must be customer-managed (HSM-backed) with strict key rotation and no plaintext keys leaving the premises.
- Air-gap compatibility: You need a process for offline model updates and reproducible install steps for offline environments.
- Compliance evidence: SOC 2 and penetration test summary required for procurement.
- Ops burden: Limited SRE headcount; prefer a deployment with clear runbooks and an option for Redwood to assist the install remotely (via a jump host under customer control).

Current stack you described
- On-prem Kubernetes (EKS Distro), Palo Alto edge, F5 load balancer, internal artifact registry, and HashiCorp Vault (HSM-stub in front of Vault).

Success criteria for pilot (your asks)
1) Proof that inference can run with KV cache disabled/enabled per policy and within accepted latency envelope (<200ms p50 for short prompts).
2) Demonstrated offline model update workflow (single file transfer + checksum).
3) HSM integration for model encryption keys and zero plaintext egress.
4) Basic audit logs integrated into SecureOps SIEM.

Proposed next steps (owner / ETA)
- We will send our security questionnaire and a short MOP template (attached).  (Owner: me)
- SecureOps to share network diagram and details for the HSM/Vault setup. (Owner: Aisha / Rajesh)
- Schedule technical kickoff with infra + security + Redwood platform engineers. Proposed slots: Tue 6/6 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 6/7 14:00–15:00 PT.
- Redwood to prepare a short air-gap installation note and list of binary/artifact hashes for transfer. (Owner: Vivek)

Attachments (stubbed)
- SecureOps_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (security questionnaire, 12 pages)
- initial-mop.xlsx (installation checklist / MOP)

Open questions we want from you
- Do you have an HSM vendor preference (Thales, AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault HSM)?
- Any blackout windows for install / PoC?

If that matches your notes, I’ll get the questionnaire back to you today and lock the kickoff once you confirm a slot.

Thanks,

--

Priyom — thanks for the thorough recap and for sending the questionnaire. A few clarifications from our side and a couple asks before we lock a kickoff: 

Confirmations / clarifications
- HSM: We currently use an on-prem Thales Luna (HSM) fronted by Vault; keys are not exportable. Any integration must support wrapping/unwrapping via a customer-side KMS.
- Offline updates: We require signed artifact delivery and an approval step from our security team for any new model binary.
- Telemetry: No telemetry may be sent outside the SecureOps network; logs should be pushed to our SIEM via a dedicated host.

Asks
1) Can Redwood provide a short (1–2 page) note on the offline-update workflow (who signs artifacts, how checksums are verified)?
2) Please attach SOC 2 Type II evidence and latest penetration test executive summary — procurement needs this for the vendor evaluation.
3) Can we schedule the kickoff for Wed 6/7 14:00–15:00 PT? That works best for our infra and security leads.

I’ve attached an internal doc that lists our procurement timelines and mandatory info (SecureOps_org_req.docx). After the kickoff we’ll aim to make a go/no-go within two weeks provided the security checklist is satisfied.

Thanks — Aisha
